task_3.title: Raise minimum dependency support and align NetCDF/HDF5 backend behavior
task_3.description: The 2022.12.0 update raises the minimum supported versions of several optional and core dependencies, including `h5py`, `hdf5`, `netcdf4`, `dask`, `distributed`, `matplotlib-base`, `packaging`, `pint`, and `typing_extensions`. With those newer dependency floors in place, the NetCDF/HDF5 backends rely on newer library behavior directly and broaden supported write-time encoding validation for compression-related settings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2022.12.0 requires the documented newer minimum dependency versions and that NetCDF/HDF5 backend behavior remains correct with those versions, including native advanced indexing support and consistent acceptance of compression-related encoding options.

expectation.grounded: The library must require at least the updated minimum versions documented in the release note, including `boto>=1.20`, `cartopy>=0.20`, `distributed>=2021.11`, `dask>=2021.11`, `h5py>=3.6`, `hdf5>=1.12`, `matplotlib-base>=3.5`, `nc-time-axis>=1.4`, `netcdf4>=1.5.7`, `packaging>=21.3`, `pint>=0.18`, `pseudonetcdf>=3.2`, and `typing_extensions>=4.0`. For HDF5-backed array access through the `h5netcdf` backend, array indexing should defer to the backend library's native handling of NumPy array indexers rather than applying a compatibility conversion. For netCDF4 variable encoding extraction, `compression` must be recognized as a valid encoding key alongside other supported encoding fields, including when validating encodings without depending on the older `h5py` gate.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users should be able to rely on the newer supported dependency stack without legacy compatibility shims. Reading data through the HDF5-backed backend should honor advanced indexers using the backend's native behavior, and writing with compression-related encoding metadata should be accepted consistently when using supported NetCDF functionality.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade must not reintroduce compatibility behavior needed only for older `h5py` releases below the new minimum. Encoding validation must continue to reject unsupported encoding keys while allowing the documented compression-related keys that are part of the public write interface. The requirement should be limited to observable dependency support and backend behavior, without depending on CI-only dependency policy checks.
constraints.conceptual: The new version should narrow support only by the published dependency floor changes and should not otherwise change backend behavior in surprising ways. Valid compression settings should work consistently, and invalid metadata should still be treated as invalid.

behavior: The supported environment for 2022.12.0 starts at the newer minimum versions listed in the release note, replacing the older dependency floor from 2022.11.0.

When arrays are accessed through the `h5netcdf` backend with NumPy-based fancy or advanced indexing, the backend now uses the underlying library's native indexing behavior instead of converting NumPy indexers into Python lists first.
When extracting or validating variable encodings for the `netCDF4` backend, the `compression` encoding field is treated as a valid supported encoding key.
Validation of variable encodings continues to distinguish between supported and unsupported encoding entries even after `compression` becomes broadly accepted.
acceptance_criteria: When a user upgrades from 2022.11.0 to 2022.12.0, the documented minimum dependency versions should match the newer floors published in the release note.

When a dataset backed by `h5netcdf` is indexed with NumPy array indexers on a supported dependency stack, the read operation should succeed using the backend's native indexing semantics rather than requiring legacy indexer coercion.

When a user supplies `compression` in variable encoding for a `netCDF4` write path, the encoding should be accepted as a supported option rather than being treated as invalid solely because of backend-specific gating.
When a user supplies unsupported encoding fields, those fields should still be rejected or filtered according to the existing encoding-validation behavior.

task_1.title: Add origin and offset support to resample
task_1.description: The upgrade extends DataArray and Dataset resampling so callers can control bin alignment with origin and offset, including for CFTimeIndex-backed time coordinates. It also defines validation and default bin-labeling behavior needed for these new alignment options.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that time-based resampling supports aligning bins with both an explicit origin and an additional offset so users can control how resample windows are anchored for regular datetime data and CF calendar data.

expectation.grounded: DataArray.resample() and Dataset.resample() must accept optional origin and offset arguments in addition to base. These arguments must be forwarded to both pandas-backed resampling and CFTimeIndex-backed resampling. For CFTimeIndex-backed resampling, origin must support the named values 'epoch', 'start', 'start_day', 'end', and 'end_day', as well as a cftime.datetime value; offset must accept a datetime.timedelta or an offset string that can be converted to a timedelta. When origin is 'end' or 'end_day', default closed and label behavior for non-month/quarter/year-end frequencies must align to the right edge. For tick-like frequencies, base may still shift bin anchoring, but base and offset cannot be supplied together.
expectation.conceptual: Resampling should let users choose the reference point used to anchor aggregation windows and optionally shift that reference by a time delta. This alignment control should work consistently across normal datetime indexes and CF calendar indexes, including backward-aligned windows based on the end of the series.

constraints.grounded: The feature must preserve existing month-end, quarter-end, and year-end default right-closed and right-labeled behavior. CFTimeIndex resampling must reject calls that provide both base and offset, must reject offset values that cannot be interpreted as a timedelta, and must reject origin values outside the supported named options or a compatible cftime.datetime. Offset handling must remain observable through resample output alignment only; loffset remains a separate label adjustment input.
constraints.conceptual: The new alignment options must not break existing end-of-period resampling defaults or blur the distinction between bin anchoring and label shifting. Invalid combinations or unsupported alignment values should fail clearly instead of being silently accepted.

behavior: Resample operations on DataArray and Dataset accept origin and offset as public parameters.
CFTimeIndex-backed resampling computes bin edges using the supplied origin and optional offset rather than relying only on base-style day anchoring.
For tick-based frequencies, base is translated into an equivalent alignment shift when used alone.
Providing both base and offset in the same resample call raises a ValueError.
Providing an offset that is neither a timedelta nor a convertible offset string raises a ValueError.
For CFTimeIndex-backed resampling, origin accepts supported named anchors or a cftime datetime value; unsupported origin values raise a ValueError.
When resampling from the series end using origin='end' or origin='end_day', default bin closure and labeling for non-month/quarter/year-end frequencies use the right edge.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls DataArray.resample() or Dataset.resample() with origin and no offset, the resampled bins should be anchored relative to the requested origin rather than only the start day.
When a user supplies offset together with a supported origin, the resampled output should shift bin boundaries by that offset for both standard datetime indexes and CF calendar indexes.

When a CF calendar time coordinate is resampled with origin set to 'epoch', 'start', 'start_day', 'end', 'end_day', or an explicit cftime datetime, the operation should succeed and align bins accordingly.
When origin is 'end' or 'end_day' for a non-month/quarter/year-end frequency and closed/label are omitted, the resulting resample buckets should default to right-closed and right-labeled behavior.
When both base and offset are supplied in the same resample call, the operation should fail with a ValueError.
When offset is not interpretable as a timedelta or supported offset string, the operation should fail with a ValueError.
When base is supplied alone for a tick-like frequency, the resulting bin alignment should reflect that base shift.

task_2.title: Add experimental Zarr v3 read/write support
task_2.description: The update adds experimental support for the in-progress Zarr v3 specification in xarray's Zarr read and write APIs. Users can now target Zarr v3 explicitly, version selection is inferred from versioned store objects when possible, ambiguous path-like stores continue to default to v2 for compatibility, and unsupported consolidated-metadata workflows are blocked for v3.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray can read and write datasets against the experimental Zarr v3 protocol while keeping existing Zarr v2 behavior stable, requiring explicit version intent when the store type does not reveal the protocol version, and preventing unsupported consolidated-metadata usage for Zarr v3.

expectation.grounded: Expose a `zarr_version` option on `xr.open_zarr`, `xr.open_dataset(..., engine='zarr')`, `Dataset.to_zarr`, and the backend `to_zarr` pathway so callers can target Zarr spec version 2 or 3. When `zarr_version` is omitted, infer it from a store object's `_store_version` when available; otherwise default to version 2 for path-like or otherwise ambiguous stores. For `zarr_version > 2`, pass the selected version through to Zarr store opening, force `consolidated=None` to behave as non-consolidated access, and reject `consolidated=True` or consolidation-on-close usage with a `ValueError` because consolidated metadata is not yet supported for Zarr v3. Reading variable metadata from Zarr v3 should avoid exposing transient `filters` metadata as user variable attributes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to opt into experimental Zarr v3 support through the normal xarray Zarr APIs. If the backing store already identifies its Zarr protocol version, xarray should follow that version automatically; if the store is just a path or URL, xarray should remain on Zarr v2 unless the caller explicitly requests v3. Zarr v3 operations should use non-consolidated metadata only, and unsupported consolidation requests should fail clearly rather than behaving inconsistently.

constraints.grounded: Existing Zarr v2 callers must remain backward compatible when no `zarr_version` is supplied. The new behavior must apply consistently across open and write entry points that delegate to the Zarr backend. For Zarr v3, callers must not be allowed to use consolidated metadata reads or writes. Observable dataset and variable metadata should not gain backend-specific `filters` attributes as an artifact of Zarr v3 support.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve current default behavior for existing users, add v3 only as an explicit or inferable capability, and block unsupported metadata modes instead of silently producing partially supported stores. User-visible metadata should stay clean and reflect data semantics rather than backend internals.

behavior: `xr.open_zarr`, `xr.open_dataset` with the Zarr engine, and `Dataset.to_zarr` accept a `zarr_version` argument that targets Zarr protocol version 2 or 3.
If no `zarr_version` is provided and the store object exposes its own version, xarray uses that store version automatically.
If no `zarr_version` is provided and the store is path-like or otherwise does not expose a version, xarray defaults to Zarr v2 for backward compatibility.
When `zarr_version=3` is requested, xarray opens the underlying Zarr group using the selected version and treats `consolidated=None` as non-consolidated operation.

When `zarr_version=3` is used with `consolidated=True` or any write path that would consolidate metadata on close, the operation raises `ValueError` instead of attempting unsupported consolidated metadata handling.
When reading Zarr metadata for variables under the new v3 support path, backend filter metadata should not appear as normal user variable attributes.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller writes or opens a dataset with a Zarr store object that identifies itself as version 3, xarray should use Zarr v3 behavior without requiring a separate version override.
When a caller writes or opens a dataset using a filesystem path or URL and does not provide `zarr_version`, the operation should continue to target Zarr v2 behavior.
When a caller passes `zarr_version=3` to `Dataset.to_zarr`, the dataset should be written through the Zarr backend using v3 semantics.
When a caller passes `zarr_version=3` to `xr.open_zarr` or `xr.open_dataset(..., engine='zarr')`, the dataset should be opened using v3 semantics.
When `zarr_version=3` is combined with `consolidated=True` during open or write, the operation should fail with `ValueError` rather than attempting consolidated metadata access.
When `zarr_version=3` is used and `consolidated` is left unset, the operation should proceed in non-consolidated mode.
When data is read from a Zarr v3-backed dataset, internal backend filter metadata should not be surfaced as ordinary variable attributes in the resulting xarray objects.

task_6.title: Restore cftime plotting via lazy nc_time_axis import
task_6.description: The upgrade fixes a regression where plotting xarray data with cftime-based time coordinates stopped working in 2022.11.0 even when the optional nc_time_axis package was installed. In 2022.12.0, xarray restores support by importing nc_time_axis only when cftime-based plotting is actually encountered, while still raising an import error when that optional dependency is unavailable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that plotting DataArray or coordinate values that use cftime-based datetimes works again when the optional nc_time_axis dependency is installed, and fails with a clear dependency error when cftime plotting is attempted without that package.

expectation.grounded: When xarray plotting paths validate plottable inputs through _ensure_plottable, arrays or coordinates containing cftime.datetime values must be accepted as plottable date-like inputs. If cftime.datetime values are present and nc_time_axis is available, xarray must import nc_time_axis at that point so Matplotlib registers cftime support before plotting proceeds. If cftime.datetime values are present and nc_time_axis is unavailable, plotting must raise ImportError rather than falling through to a Matplotlib type conversion failure. Existing acceptance of numeric, boolean, string, numpy datetime64, numpy timedelta64, and datetime.datetime plotting inputs must remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: Plots that use non-standard calendar dates from cftime should work again out of the box whenever the optional nc_time_axis package is installed. If that package is missing, the plotting call should stop with an explicit missing-dependency error instead of an unrelated low-level plotting failure. Plotting behavior for standard supported coordinate types should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not require eager import of nc_time_axis for all plotting usage. Only cftime.datetime plotting should trigger the optional dependency import check. Inputs already recognized as plottable through supported numpy dtypes or datetime.datetime must continue to pass validation without new dependency requirements, and unsupported coordinate/value dtypes must still raise TypeError.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to cftime-based plotting. It should not make ordinary plotting depend on extra packages, and it should preserve existing validation rules for supported and unsupported plot input types.

behavior: xarray plotting treats cftime.datetime values as valid date-like plotting inputs during plottability checks.
When cftime.datetime values are about to be plotted and nc_time_axis is installed, xarray loads that package so Matplotlib can handle cftime axes correctly.
When cftime.datetime values are plotted without nc_time_axis installed, xarray raises ImportError indicating that the optional dependency is required.
For non-cftime supported plotting inputs such as numeric, boolean, string, numpy datetime64, numpy timedelta64, and datetime.datetime values, validation behavior remains unchanged.
Unsupported plotting input dtypes continue to fail validation with TypeError rather than being treated as plottable.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray uses a cftime-based time coordinate and nc_time_axis is installed, calling the xarray plotting API should succeed without a Matplotlib float-conversion error.
When plotting cftime.datetime coordinate or value data and nc_time_axis is not installed, the plotting API should raise ImportError identifying the optional dependency requirement.
When plotting arrays with supported non-cftime coordinate/value types, the plotting API should behave as before and must not require nc_time_axis.
When plotting arrays with unsupported coordinate/value types, xarray should continue to reject them with TypeError during plottability validation.

task_5.title: Preserve source attributes in xr.where with keep_attrs
task_5.description: The upgrade fixes xarray.where so that enabling keep_attrs preserves metadata from the x input consistently, including coordinate attributes and mixed DataArray/Dataset cases, instead of incorrectly overwriting coordinate metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `xr.where(..., keep_attrs=True)` preserves the metadata of the `x` input in the returned object, including coordinate attributes, and handles DataArray, Dataset, and scalar combinations without incorrectly copying unrelated attributes.

expectation.grounded: When `xr.where` is called with `keep_attrs=True`, the result should rebuild attributes from the second argument `x` at the appropriate output level. For DataArray results, the returned array attrs and coordinate attrs should come from `x`. For Dataset results, dataset-level attrs should come from `x` when `x` is a Dataset, data variable attrs should come from matching variables on `x` when available, and coordinate attrs should come from matching coordinates on `x`. If `x` is scalar-like and has no attrs, the result should not synthesize attrs. When `y` is a Dataset and `x` is not, promotion of `x` to a Dataset should still preserve attrs only for the matching promoted variable from `x`, while leaving dataset-level attrs empty.
expectation.conceptual: Turning on attribute preservation for `xr.where` should keep metadata aligned with the values selected from the primary `x` input. The returned object should preserve the source metadata that users expect to follow those values, especially coordinate metadata, and should avoid inventing or misassigning attrs when one side is a scalar or when the result is promoted to a Dataset.

constraints.grounded: The fix must remain consistent with `DataArray.where` and `Dataset.where` semantics that `keep_attrs=True` keeps attrs from `x`, not from `y` or `cond`. Coordinate attrs must not be overwritten by variable attrs. Scalar inputs must continue to be accepted without attribute lookup failures. Mixed Dataset/DataArray inputs must preserve only attrs that can be sourced from matching objects on `x`.
constraints.conceptual: Attribute preservation should be predictable, source-based, and safe across supported input combinations. The behavior must not regress by attaching metadata from the wrong operand or by failing on scalar cases.

behavior: `xr.where(..., keep_attrs=True)` now preserves coordinate attributes from `x` instead of replacing them with variable attributes.
For DataArray outputs, attrs on the returned array and its coordinates follow the `x` input when `keep_attrs=True`.
For Dataset outputs, dataset-level attrs come from `x` when `x` is a Dataset, and variable-level attrs come from matching variables on `x` when present.
When `y` is a Dataset and `x` is a DataArray, the promoted Dataset result keeps attrs only on the matching data variable from `x`, while dataset-level attrs remain empty.
When `x` is scalar-like, `keep_attrs=True` does not fabricate attrs on the result and continues to work without errors.
acceptance_criteria: When `xr.where` is called with DataArray inputs and `keep_attrs=True`, it should return a DataArray whose attrs and coordinate attrs match those of `x`.
When `xr.where` is called with `keep_attrs=True` and `x` is scalar-like, it should return the correct values without adding attrs that are not present on `x`.
When `xr.where` returns a Dataset and `x` is a Dataset, it should preserve dataset attrs, matching data variable attrs, and coordinate attrs from `x`.

When `xr.where` returns a Dataset because `y` is a Dataset but `x` is not, it should preserve attrs only for the promoted variable corresponding to `x` and should not populate unrelated dataset-level attrs.
When coordinates are present on the result, their attrs should reflect the matching coordinates from `x` rather than attrs copied from data variables.

task_4.title: Deprecate the PyNIO backend with runtime warnings
task_4.description: Version 2022.12.0 formally deprecates the PyNIO backend. Applications that still open datasets through the PyNIO integration should continue to work for now, but they must surface a deprecation warning at runtime so users know the backend is no longer supported and will be removed in a future release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using the PyNIO backend is treated as deprecated while remaining temporarily usable, so users are explicitly informed that this backend is no longer supported and will be removed in a future release.

expectation.grounded: When the PyNIO backend is invoked through the xarray PyNIO integration, including construction of `NioDataStore` and dataset opening through the `PynioBackendEntrypoint`, xarray should emit a `DeprecationWarning` indicating that the PyNIO backend is deprecated and scheduled for future removal. The backend should still report availability based on the `Nio` module and continue opening datasets as before apart from the warning.
expectation.conceptual: Users who still rely on the PyNIO engine should see a clear deprecation signal whenever they use it, while existing reads continue to behave the same in this release. The library should communicate that PyNIO support is on a removal path without silently changing successful usage into a failure.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove the PyNIO backend in this release. Preserve existing backend availability detection and dataset-opening behavior, with the new observable change limited to deprecation signaling during PyNIO-backed access.
constraints.conceptual: The update should warn, not break. Existing PyNIO users must still be able to open supported datasets in the current release, but they should no longer be able to use the backend without being told it is deprecated.

behavior: Using `NioDataStore` now emits a `DeprecationWarning` before proceeding with normal PyNIO-backed access.
The public PyNIO backend entrypoint is explicitly marked as deprecated for users discovering or selecting backends.
PyNIO backend availability remains conditional on whether the `Nio` module is installed.
Dataset opening through the PyNIO backend continues to function in this release aside from the added deprecation warning.
acceptance_criteria: When an application opens data through xarray's PyNIO backend, it should receive a `DeprecationWarning` indicating that PyNIO support will be removed in a future release.
When `NioDataStore` is instantiated for PyNIO-backed access, it should still initialize and allow normal use after issuing the deprecation warning.
When the `Nio` dependency is present, PyNIO backend availability should remain exposed to users in the same way as before.
When a user relies on the PyNIO backend in 2022.12.0, the observable behavior change should be the deprecation notice rather than immediate backend removal or a new incompatibility.

task_7.title: Fix xr.polyval static return type inference
task_7.description: The upgrade corrects xarray's public type information for xr.polyval so static type checkers can infer the result type from the input combination, including common calls that rely on the default degree_dim argument. This removes overly broad union typing and makes the annotated API match the documented DataArray-versus-Dataset behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xr.polyval exposes accurate static typing so users upgrading to 2022.12.0 get the correct inferred return type based on whether coord and coeffs are DataArray or Dataset inputs, including when degree_dim is not passed.

expectation.grounded: xr.polyval should provide overloads whose defaulted degree_dim parameter matches the callable signature, allowing type checkers to resolve the return type precisely: DataArray when coord and coeffs are both DataArray, and Dataset whenever either coord or coeffs is a Dataset.
expectation.conceptual: Calling xr.polyval should no longer produce an unnecessarily ambiguous inferred type in static analysis. The reported return type should reflect the kind of xarray objects passed by the user, even in the common case where optional arguments are omitted.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve the existing public xr.polyval call pattern, including omission of degree_dim, while narrowing only the static return annotation semantics for supported DataArray and Dataset input combinations. It must not require callers to add arguments solely to satisfy typing.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve developer tooling feedback without changing how users normally call the API or introducing new calling requirements.

behavior: Static analysis of xr.polyval(coord: DataArray, coeffs: DataArray) should resolve to DataArray when degree_dim is omitted.
Static analysis of xr.polyval with either coord or coeffs as Dataset should resolve to Dataset when degree_dim is omitted.
Providing degree_dim explicitly should preserve the same return-type mapping across DataArray and Dataset input combinations.
The annotated API should avoid broad union return types for input combinations whose result type is deterministically known from the public signature.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls xr.polyval with a DataArray coordinate and DataArray coefficients, static type checkers should infer a DataArray result.
When a user calls xr.polyval with a Dataset coordinate and DataArray coefficients, static type checkers should infer a Dataset result.
When a user calls xr.polyval with a DataArray coordinate and Dataset coefficients, static type checkers should infer a Dataset result.
When a user calls xr.polyval with Dataset inputs for both coord and coeffs, static type checkers should infer a Dataset result.
When the user omits degree_dim in any supported call above, the inferred return type should remain the precise type for that input combination rather than a generic union.

task_9.title: Preserve existing coordinate indexes during Dataset.assign_coords
task_9.description: Upgrading to 2022.12.0 fixes a regression in xarray where `Dataset.assign_coords()` could replace existing dimension-coordinate indexes with default pandas indexes while adding or updating coordinates. The update preserves unchanged indexes, including custom index types, so coordinate assignment no longer silently alters index semantics on unrelated dimensions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `Dataset.assign_coords()` preserves the existing indexes of dimension coordinates that are not being updated, and does not reset unaffected or retained coordinates to a default pandas index when coordinates are added or reassigned.

expectation.grounded: When `xarray.Dataset.assign_coords()` merges new coordinate values into a dataset, existing dimension-coordinate indexes must be carried through the merge and alignment process instead of being replaced by default pandas indexes. This applies to untouched coordinates and to coordinates that remain after operations involving multi-coordinate indexes. Existing custom index classes exposed through xarray indexes should remain associated with their coordinates unless that coordinate's index is explicitly replaced by the assignment itself.
expectation.conceptual: Assigning coordinates should only change the coordinates the user is actually assigning. Other dimension indexes should stay the same, including any custom or non-default index behavior, so adding a coordinate does not unexpectedly change how existing dimensions are indexed.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve observable index identity and type semantics for unaffected dimension coordinates across coordinate assignment. Coordinate alignment and merge behavior must continue honoring the dataset's existing indexes rather than reconstructing fallback default indexes for retained coordinates.
constraints.conceptual: The update must avoid regressions where unrelated dimensions change indexing behavior as a side effect of assigning coordinates. Existing indexing behavior should remain stable unless the user explicitly changes that coordinate's index.

behavior: `Dataset.assign_coords()` no longer resets preserved dimension coordinates to a default pandas index when adding or updating other coordinates.
Datasets using custom xarray index implementations on a dimension retain those custom index types after assigning unrelated coordinates.
Coordinate merge and alignment during assignment respect the dataset's existing index mappings for retained coordinates.

Coordinates unaffected by the assignment continue to expose the same indexing semantics after the operation, including in cases involving multi-coordinate indexes where only part of the indexed coordinate set is changed or dropped.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset has a non-default or custom index on a dimension and `assign_coords()` is used to add an unrelated coordinate, the resulting dataset should preserve that dimension's existing index type instead of converting it to a default pandas index.
When `assign_coords()` updates some coordinates but leaves other dimension coordinates untouched, the untouched coordinates should retain their previous index behavior in the returned dataset.

When coordinate assignment interacts with coordinates associated with a multi-coordinate index, any retained coordinates not explicitly replaced should keep their existing index semantics rather than being rebuilt as default indexes.
After coordinate assignment, users should observe index preservation as part of normal dataset indexing metadata, with no silent downgrade of unaffected dimensions to default indexing behavior.

task_10.title: Document netCDF group read/write workflow
task_10.description: The 2022.12.0 update adds user-facing documentation showing how to read from and write to individual groups within a single netCDF file. The change improves discoverability of an existing I/O workflow rather than changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the I/O documentation explains how users can read and write individual groups within a single netCDF file.

expectation.grounded: The netCDF I/O documentation should include an example-based description of working with individual groups in one netCDF file, covering both writing data to a group and reading data back from a group.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to find clear guidance that demonstrates the full workflow for targeting specific groups inside a netCDF file, so grouped data layouts are understandable and discoverable from the docs alone.

constraints.grounded: The update should be limited to user-facing documentation for netCDF group I/O behavior. No new runtime APIs, behavior changes, or error-handling changes are evidenced by the provided materials.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should clarify existing capabilities without altering how the library executes I/O operations in production.

behavior: The documentation now covers writing to an individual group within a netCDF file.
The documentation now covers reading from an individual group within a netCDF file.
The documented workflow treats multiple groups as content that can coexist within a single netCDF file.
The change is documentation-only based on the provided artifacts and does not indicate a runtime semantic change.
acceptance_criteria: When a user consults the netCDF I/O documentation, they should find an example that shows how to write data to a specific group in a netCDF file.
When a user consults the netCDF I/O documentation, they should find an example that shows how to read data from a specific group in a netCDF file.
The documented examples should make it clear that multiple individual groups can be addressed within the same netCDF file.
The upgrade should not require users to account for any new runtime behavior beyond the newly documented usage guidance.

task_8.title: Automatically rewind file-like inputs before engine detection
task_8.description: The upgrade changes how file-like inputs are handled when opening datasets. Reusing the same stream, including fsspec-backed S3 file objects, should no longer fail just because its read pointer is not at the beginning. The library now rewinds eligible file objects before reading the file signature, improving compatibility for repeated opens and other non-zero-position stream inputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that opening a dataset from a reusable file-like object does not fail solely because the stream position is not at the beginning, including when the same fsspec-backed S3 file object is opened multiple times.

expectation.grounded: When dataset opening relies on reading a magic number from an `io.IOBase` file-like object, the library should automatically seek the stream to position 0 before reading if `tell()` reports a non-zero position, then restore the stream to position 0 afterward. Reusing the same file object with APIs such as `open_dataset` should therefore no longer raise the previous pointer-position `ValueError` during engine detection. Unsupported non-sliceable and non-`io.IOBase` inputs should still raise `TypeError`.
expectation.conceptual: Opening a dataset from a file object should be resilient to the file pointer already having moved. Users should be able to reuse the same compatible stream object without manually closing and reopening it just to reset its position.

constraints.grounded: This change applies to file-like inputs handled as `io.IOBase` during file-signature inspection. The stream should remain positioned at the beginning after signature reading. Existing behavior for byte-like or sliceable inputs remains unchanged, and unsupported input types must still fail with `TypeError` rather than being silently accepted.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only relax failures caused by stream position, without broadening accepted input categories or leaving streams in an unexpected state after opening logic inspects them.

behavior: If a compatible file-like object is not at position 0 when the library inspects its file signature, the library rewinds it instead of failing immediately.
After reading the initial signature bytes from a compatible file-like object, the library leaves that object positioned at the beginning of the stream.
Repeated dataset opens against the same compatible file object can proceed without requiring the caller to reopen the stream first.
Inputs that are neither sliceable byte-like objects nor `io.IOBase` file-like objects continue to be rejected with `TypeError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user passes the same compatible file-like object to `open_dataset` more than once, each open should be able to proceed without a pointer-position error caused solely by prior reads.
When a compatible file-like object has already been advanced before dataset opening begins, the library should rewind it automatically and continue signature detection.
When dataset opening inspects a compatible file-like object, the object should be at position 0 after inspection completes.
When a caller provides an unsupported input type that is neither a compatible file-like object nor a sliceable byte-like source, the library should still reject it with `TypeError`.
